answer: Coordinated Pulse Windows. Each epoch, every identity must submit a distinct transaction during a randomly assigned 200ms pulse window derived from its key; duplicates or misses count as zero. An identity joins the active set only if its pulse history forms a long-lived vertex in the trust graph. To sustain N clones, an attacker must run N independently clocked clients, each anchored to the epoch schedule, costing full node infrastructure per identity rather than one shared client.
